sources.title: Constitution of Tonga, 2020 Revised Edition

claims.text: Clauses 30 and 41 describe a constitutional monarchy; royal signature is required for legislation. Clause 36 assigns military command to the King but requires Assembly consent for war.

The King appoints the Assembly-recommended elected representative as prime minister. Cabinet exercises executive authority collectively and answers to the Assembly; ministers are nominated by the prime minister and appointed by the King. Reserved royal powers are excluded.
The King appoints Privy Council advisers. The Council also handles specified hereditary estate and title appeals.
The Assembly includes nobles' representatives, people's representatives and Cabinet. Its recommended Speaker must be an elected nobles' representative and is appointed by the King.

sources.scope_note: Consolidated edition, not a complete amendment or commencement ledger. Do not backdate these provisions to 1990 or assume no later amendments.

sources.title: Act of Constitution of Tonga, older revised text

claims.text: The older text gives the King appointment of ministers, serving at his pleasure or for their commission period. Ministers sit in the Privy Council and Assembly.
The older text includes Privy Councillors and Cabinet in the Assembly, specifies nine noble and nine people's elected representatives, and gives the King appointment of the Speaker.

sources.scope_note: The volume carries a 1988 Revised Edition label but includes later amendment notes, including Act 12 of 1990. It is not accepted as an exact 1 January 1990 legal snapshot.

sources.title: Act of Constitution of Tonga (Amendment) (No.2) Act 2010, Act 20

claims.text: Act 20 replaces the prime minister, Cabinet, Privy Council, Assembly-composition and Speaker provisions. It changes the English description of royal government from governing to reigning.
The printed Act records Assembly passage on 20 July 2010. Passage alone does not establish commencement.

sources.scope_note: The extracted assent line has no legible date. The separate Assembly explanatory note supplies assent and procedure dates.

sources.title: Interim Speaker clarifies nomination and appointment of the Prime Minister

claims.text: The Assembly explanatory note dates royal assent to Act 20 to 24 November 2010. It dates the return of election writs to 2 December 2010, starting the Schedule's nomination procedure except the interim Speaker appointment.
claims.uncertainty: This procedural commencement statement does not establish the effective date of every amendment.

sources.title: How Parliament works?

The page describes Tonga as lacking a political party system. This is a description of parliamentary arrangements, not an exhaustive register establishing the absence of political organizations.
claims.uncertainty: Independent candidacy and informal opposition must not erase separately documented parties.

sources.scope_note: Date is the page's last update. Prefer the Constitution for formal appointment powers where explanatory shorthand differs.

claims.uncertainty: A procedural notice issued before the selection. It records no result and no appointment or effective date for a Prime Minister. The interim Speaker appointment is not imported as a Speaker holder observation.

sources.title: King appoints Prime Minister Hon. Siaosi 'Ofakivahafolau Sovaleni
sources.publisher: Prime Minister's Office, Government of Tonga

claims.text: The PMO's English release dated 28 December 2021 states that, in accordance with Clause 50A of the Constitution, King Tupou VI appointed the Prime Minister-Designate, Hon. Siaosi 'Ofakivahafolau Sovaleni, as Prime Minister of Tonga with effect from 27 December 2021.
claims.locator: Release image, date line under 'MEDIA RELEASE' and first body paragraph
claims.uncertainty: The stated effective date only. The release does not give the date on which the Royal Warrant was signed or presented, and its own 28 December date is not read as either. No end date, term length or caretaker arrangement is stated or inferred.

claims.text: The same release states that Sovaleni was elected as Prime Minister by the Legislative Assembly on 15 December, following the 2021 General Election. The printed sentence begins 'Prior to being elected' and ends by saying he will be the 18th Prime Minister of Tonga.
claims.uncertainty: Only the dated Assembly election is used; it is the Assembly's selection, not the royal appointment. The sentence is recorded as printed, and its ordinal is not used to number or complete a succession.

sources.scope_note: English media release dated 28 December 2021, published on the PMO page as one JPEG image (NewPrimeMinister2021.jpg). The release date is publication, not the warrant's signature or presentation date, which the release does not give. Its undated remark on the Prime Minister's earlier portfolios and its forecast of a 29 December Cabinet announcement are not imported. A direct non-browser request for the page returned HTTP 403; the page HTML hash is not asserted.

sources.title: Fakanofo 'e he 'Ene 'Afio 'a Hon. Siaosi 'Ofakivahafolau Sovaleni ko e Palēmia 'o Tonga
sources.publisher: Prime Minister's Office, Government of Tonga (Pule'anga Tonga)

claims.text: The PMO's Tongan-language release dated 'Aho 28 'o Tisema 2021 states that King Tupou VI appointed Hon. Siaosi 'Ofakivahafolau Sovaleni (Hu'akavameiliku) as Palēmia (Prime Minister) of Tonga, as recommended by the Fale Alea, under clause (kupu) 50A of the Constitution. It states that the premiership is reckoned from the day of appointment, which it gives as 27 Tisema 2021.
claims.locator: Release image, date line under 'ONGOONGO TUKUATU' and first and second body paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: The English rendering is this packet's reading, not an official translation. Hu'akavameiliku is printed in parentheses as a name form; no chiefly-title grant, date or rank is inferred. Read with the English release's 'with effect from', 27 Tisema is the effective date; neither release records the warrant's signature or presentation as a separate event.

sources.scope_note: Tongan-language counterpart of the English release, published on its own PMO page as one JPEG image (newprimeminister2.jpg). Its third paragraph expects the Cabinet announcement 'apongipongi (tomorrow), Pulelulu 29 Tisema 2021, consistent with issue on 28 December; that forecast is not imported. A direct non-browser request for the page returned HTTP 403; the page HTML hash is not asserted.

sources.title: Prime Minister, Hon. Siaosi 'Ofakivahafolau Sovaleni announces new Cabinet Ministers
sources.publisher: Prime Minister's Office, Government of Tonga

claims.text: The PMO's release dated 29 December 2021 states that King Tupou VI, on the Prime Minister's recommendations, appointed the new Ministers of Government with effect from 28 December 2021. Its numbered list of twelve Cabinet members gives (1) Hon. Siaosi 'Ofakivahafolau Sovaleni as Prime Minister and Minister for Education and Training, for Police, Fire Services and Emergency Services, and for His Majesty's Armed Forces, and (2) Hon. Poasi Mataele Tei as Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for MEIDECC and Minister for Public Enterprises.
claims.locator: Release image 1 (page 1): first paragraph and list items 1-2; the list ends at item 12 on image 2
claims.uncertainty: The stated effective date of the ministerial appointments, not the date letters were presented or oaths taken. It is not read as a second start date for the premiership, which the 28 December releases give as 27 December. Items 3-12 are not imported as holder observations, and the list is not asserted to remain unchanged.

claims.text: The same release states that the Prime Minister presented the letters of appointment to all of the Cabinet Ministers, including the Governor of Ha'apai, 'today, Wednesday 29th December, 2021', that the first Cabinet meeting was convened that day, and that all of the Cabinet Ministers took their Ministerial oath.
claims.locator: Release image 2 (page 2): the three paragraphs after list item 12
claims.uncertainty: The oath sentence follows two sentences dated 'today' and carries no date of its own; it is read as part of the 29 December report. Letter presentation and oath are separate from the 28 December effective date. Ministers' letters of appointment are not the Royal Warrant appointing the Prime Minister.

sources.scope_note: Published on the PMO page as two JPEG page images (primeminister-2021.jpg and primeminister-2021-1-1.jpg). The group photograph on image 2 is not used for identification, likeness or portrait work. The Governor of Ha'apai is mentioned, not named, and is not imported.
